_note: v5.10: v5.8 + ONE change, PLID-style multiple descriptions per class (Bao et al., ECCV 2024, 'Prompting Language-Informed Distribution'). PLID represents each class by several LLM-written descriptions instead of one, so the class embedding covers more of how the disease can look. Here every disease gets its 2-3 existing visual descriptions (short, long, contrastive) and the class embedding is their mean. Differs from v5.7 (val -1.3), which paired one taxonomy sentence with one visual sentence: this uses visual text only. Not full PLID (no Gaussian class distributions, no decision fusion). Compare with v5.8 (v5.5 recipe, same 3 validation splits, seeds 42-44): mean validation HM 59.75% (per split 56.48 / 62.10 / 60.66); keep only if the mean beats it by more than 2 points (> 61.75), ideally on every split. Never decide on test.
_result: No gain: not kept. Mean validation HM 60.69% over 3 splits vs v5.8 59.75% (+0.94, needed > 61.75%). Per split 59.34 / 60.44 / 62.30 vs v5.8 56.48 / 62.10 / 60.66. Epoch 8, gamma 0.075. Test (reported only): HM 66.94% (seen 55.90, unseen 83.43). Cost: 205 min, about 215 s per epoch (roughly twice v5.13), so no v5.15 (v5.13 + descriptions) was made.
title: multi_description

model._note: Same OpenAI CLIP ViT-B/16 (QuickGELU) as v4.1/v4.2; the text encoder stays frozen.

image_encoder._note: From v5.3: v5 + more LoRA capacity: last 8 blocks instead of 4, rank 16 instead of 8. alpha 16 -> 32 keeps the LoRA scale (alpha/rank) at 2, so only capacity changes, not the effective step size. About 4x more adapter parameters (1.57M vs 393k). Same lr.

input._note: Images come from the 256 px resize cache (runs/cache/resized_256, shared with the CNN baselines). Test: CLIP's resize 224 + centre crop + CLIP mean/std. The app must standardise uploads the same way (dpd/resize_cache.standardise).

augmentation._note: Same as the CNN baselines except a milder crop scale (0.5-1 instead of 0.25-1), because CLIP's pretrained features expect whole-object views. No hue jitter: colour is diagnostic.

prompts._note: CHANGED (v5.10): descriptions_file -> disease_descriptions_multi_visual_v1.json (2-3 visual descriptions per disease: short v1, long v1, and the contrastive rewrite where one exists). Each pair / disease embedding is the renormalised mean of one sentence per description (list descriptions in dpd/prompt_learner.py). Templates unchanged.

validation._note: Same procedure as v4.2 but 1 split instead of 3: each split is now a full training run with the image encoder in the loop (images instead of cached embeddings). Note v4.2 showed one split can mis-set gamma, so treat v5's gamma with that caveat. v5.8: n_splits 1 -> 3 (seeds seed, seed+1, seed+2); selection uses the mean validation HM over splits, as in v4.2.

training._note: Prompt vectors as v4.2 (AdamW lr 2e-4, weight decay 0, logit scale 100, loss weights pair 1 / crop 0.5 / disease 0.5). max_epochs 30 -> 15 (v4.1/v4.2 selected epochs 13-18 with cached features; each epoch now re-encodes every image). Batch 256 -> 64 for GPU memory with gradients through 4 image-encoder blocks.

runtime._note: Gradient checkpointing on the text encoder as before. 4 dataloader workers read the resize cache. CHANGED (v5.10): grad_checkpointing_image true. Compute only (same results up to GPU nondeterminism): the 2-3 sentences per class more than double the text sequences per step (747 pair + 383 disease), and without it a smoke test peaked at 6.3 GiB on the 6 GiB GPU (spilled to shared memory, ~10x slower).
